title: List Basics
lesson:
## Lists

Lists are ordered, mutable collections that can hold any type of data.

### Creating Lists
```python
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
mixed = [1, "hello", 3.14, True]
empty = []
```

### Indexing and Slicing
```python
nums = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
print(nums[0])    # 10 — first element
print(nums[-1])   # 50 — last element
print(nums[1:3])  # [20, 30] — slice
print(nums[::-1]) # [50, 40, 30, 20, 10] — reversed
```

### Common Methods
```python
nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
nums.append(9)      # add to end: [3,1,4,1,5,9]
nums.insert(0, 7)   # insert at index 0
nums.remove(1)      # remove first occurrence of 1
popped = nums.pop() # remove and return last element
nums.sort()         # sort in place
print(len(nums))    # length
print(sum(nums))    # sum of all elements
print(3 in nums)    # True if 3 is in list
```

### Looping Over a List
```python
for item in nums:
    print(item)

for i, item in enumerate(nums):
    print(i, item)  # index and value
```
